3. As the Tribunal had disposed of the cases by way of a common order, hence, this Court is also disposing of the matters by way of a common order.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the accident had taken place in the year 2018 and the Tribunal had taken notional income of Rs.9,000/- per month, which is on the lower side.
It is submitted that the notional income should have taken as Rs.12,500/-.
5. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the Tribunal had rightly taken the notional income and granted the compensation.
NC: 2025:KHC:25070 HC-KAR 6.
The accident had taken place in the year 2018.
As per the table prepared to Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, notional income for the year 2018 is Rs.12,500/-.
Hence, submission of the learned counsel for the claimants is taken into consideration.

7. Accordingly, this Court is granting compensation as below:
MFA.No.6050/2022 arising out of MVC.No.5902/2018 8.
The deceased was aged 58 years at the time of accident.
Considering the age, the future prospects at 10% would be added, which comes to Rs.1,250/- i.e., Rs.13,750/-.

As there are three dependents,
1/3rd has to be deducted, it comes to Rs.9,167/-, then towards loss of dependency it would come to an amount of Rs.9,90,036/- (Rs.9,167X12X9).
For three dependents, i.e. wife and sons, under the head of loss of consortium, this Court is granting an amount of Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.44,000 X 3).

Towards funeral expenses, this Court is granting an amount of Rs.36,000/-.
9.
